Thought: I need to determine which statements about oxalates are true based on my knowledge of chemistry. Let me analyze each option:

A. They are found in nature in certain plants - Oxalates (salts of oxalic acid) are indeed found naturally in many plants including spinach, rhubarb, and other leafy greens. Plants produce oxalates as part of their natural processes.

B. They are used in rust and ink stain removers - Oxalic acid and its salts are commonly used as cleaning agents, particularly for removing rust and ink stains. They are effective at removing metal oxides and various stains.

C. They can clog kidney tubules - Oxalates can combine with calcium in the body to form calcium oxalate crystals, which are the most common component of kidney stones. These crystals can accumulate in kidney tubules and cause blockages.

Based on my knowledge, all three statements appear to be true. Oxalates are found in plants, used in cleaning products, and can cause kidney issues.
